title: Linear Algebra and Geometry
description: Vectors, distances, projections, matrices, and linear decision boundaries.
objectives: Calculate dot products, norms, and projections.
Determine the dimensions and entries of matrix products.
Interpret weights and bias geometrically in a linear model.

title: Optimization and Search
description: Search spaces, local optima, hill climbing, simulated annealing, and gradient methods.
objectives: Distinguish discrete and continuous search spaces.
Compare hill climbing, random restarts, and simulated annealing.
Carry out a gradient step and reason about local optima.

title: Supervised Learning and kNN
description: Data representations, distance metrics, neighbour voting, and choosing k.
objectives: Calculate distances and determine the outcome of neighbour voting.
Explain how scaling, k, and weighting affect predictions.
Choose model settings without using the final test set.

title: Perceptrons and Linear Regression
description: Linear models, thresholds, learning rules, MSE, and gradient updates.
objectives: Interpret linear decision boundaries and perceptron updates.
Calculate MSE, RMSE, and gradients for linear regression.
Explain the limitations of linear classifiers on non-linearly separable data.

title: Evolutionary Algorithms
description: Representations, fitness, variation, randomness, and valid genotypes.
objectives: Match problem representations to valid variation operators.
Calculate expected mutation counts and simple crossover outcomes.
Explain selection pressure, diversity, and stochastic evaluation.

title: Population Management and Applications
description: Selection, replacement, diversity, differential evolution, and wrapper search.
objectives: Compare parent selection and survivor selection strategies.
Work through differential evolution and calculate penalised wrapper objectives.
Choose validation and diversity mechanisms for applied search problems.

title: Logistic Regression and Multiclass Classification
description: Sigmoid, cross-entropy, gradients, one-vs-rest, and softmax.
objectives: Convert logits to sigmoid or softmax probabilities.
Calculate cross-entropy and a gradient update.
Distinguish binary, multiclass, and multilabel classification.

title: Neural Networks and Backpropagation
description: Hidden layers, forward passes, the chain rule, and gradient computation.
objectives: Follow a forward pass and count network parameters.
Use the chain rule to calculate gradients through hidden layers.
Distinguish gradient calculation, optimisation, and gradient checking.

title: Evaluation and Generalization
description: Data splits, cross-validation, error metrics, class imbalance, and generalisation.
objectives: Plan data splits and cross-validation without information leakage.
Calculate and interpret precision, recall, F1, and ROC curves under class imbalance.
Analyse computational cost, the bias–variance trade-off, and learning curves.

title: Regularization and Ensembles
description: L1, L2, feature selection, early stopping, bagging, and boosting.
objectives: Calculate L1 and L2 penalties and explain their effects.
Use feature selection and early stopping without data leakage.
Compare when bagging and boosting can help.

title: Deep Learning
description: Deep networks, ReLU, convolutions, residual connections, RNNs, and embeddings.
objectives: Explain saturation, ReLU, and residual connections.
Calculate convolution, pooling, and recurrent state updates.
Describe weight sharing, embeddings, and autoregressive language-model training.

title: Unsupervised Learning
description: Hierarchical clustering, k-means, autoencoders, and dimensionality reduction.
objectives: Interpret dendrograms and calculate distances between clusters under different linkage rules.
Perform assignment and update steps in k-means and calculate WCSS.
Explain reconstruction in autoencoders and choose between PCA and t-SNE.

title: Reinforcement Learning
description: Trial-exam questions on reward, Q-learning, and action selection.
objectives: Explain delayed rewards and cumulative return.
Compare Q-learning, epsilon-greedy exploration, and softmax action selection.
